claims.text: The target material is an as-cast HfNbTiVAl10 high-entropy alloy.
As-cast HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure with well-defined grain boundaries, phase distributions, and heterointerfaces.
In situ TEM during tensile deformation can directly observe and quantify heterointerface evolution and defect-propagation kinetics.
In situ TEM can directly quantify interfacial energies during controlled tensile deformation.
Heterointerface evolution, including grain-boundary sliding, microcrack initiation, and defect propagation, governs the initiation of plasticity and fracture.
Dynamic measurements of interface evolution can supply interfacial characteristics for calibration of a multiscale mechanical model.
Replacing assumed static interfacial properties with measured time-dependent behavior minimizes simulation uncertainty.
Time-dependent interfacial behavior directly affects the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
The calibrated model will predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture-related behavior with about 15% less error than established simulation protocols.
The calibrated model will reduce computational prediction time by roughly 50% relative to full-scale conventional simulations.
Established simulation workflows use pre-characterized static properties without real-time correction for evolving microstructural features.
Noisy in situ TEM data may prevent the proposed improvement in prediction.
Extreme strain localization or temperature fluctuations may alter heterointerface evolution and disrupt its correlation with macroscopic mechanical properties.
Heterointerface observations made in a TEM specimen may not scale reliably to larger sample volumes.
Variability in heterostructure morphology may reduce the consistency of the predictive gains.
Independent tensile and fracture tests can evaluate predictions of Young's modulus, yield strength, fracture toughness, and crack propagation.
Failure to reduce predictive error by at least 15%, or failure to reduce computational time by approximately 50%, is declared to falsify the hypothesis.
